title: Profiling of RNA-binding protein binding sites by in situ reverse transcription-based sequencing

title: Profiling lariat intermediates reveals genetic determinants of early and late co-transcriptional splicing
boundary: Chromatin-associated RNA is isolated with splicing suppressed, linear RNA is degraded, and UMI-bearing3prime adapter capture plus RT stopping at the2prime–5prime branch linkage recovers nascent/excised lariat tails. Paired branchpoint and nascent transcript-end information differs from native linear nascent-end preparations and incidental lariat detection in ordinary RNA-seq.

title: Rapid and Scalable Profiling of Nascent RNA with fastGRO
boundary: Nuclear run-on incorporates4-thio-UTP; fragmented newly made RNA is reversibly biotinylated and streptavidin-purified, then reducing elution feeds directional RNA-library preparation. This physical labeling/capture route differs from GRO BrUTP immunocapture, PRO biotin-NTP terminal capture and TT-seq in-vivo metabolic labeling. Standard and low-input branches are one candidate, not two.
